questions.q:
When did the Congress pass the proposal of
independence of India for the ﬁ rst time?
questions.explanation:
Congress had given an ultimatum in its Calcutta Session
(1928 A.D.) to the British Government to accept the ‘Nehru
Report’ within the year or face the mass Movement to be
launched by Congress. But the British Government did not
notice the warning. As a result, the historic Lahore Session in
the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru was held in December,
1929 A.D. and the proposal to India’s Independence had
been declared by him for the ﬁ rst time. Jawaharlal Nehru on
December 31, 1929 hoisted the ﬂ ag of India’s Independence
on the bank of Ravi river at Lahore. Congress in its meeting
of January 2, 1930 decided that the ‘Complete Independence
Day’ will be celebrated on January 26, 1930 and January 26,
of every year, will be celebrated as ‘Purna Swadhinta Divas’

questions.q:
The Lahore Session of the Indian National Congress
(1929) is very important in history, because –
1. The Congress passed a resolution demanding
complete independence.
2. The rift between the extremists and moderates was
resolved in that Session.
3. A resolution was passed rejecting the two-nation
theory in that session.
Which of the statement (s) given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The historic Lahore session of Indian National Congress in
the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru was held in December,
1929 A.D. and the proposal to India’s complete independence
(Purna Swaraj) had been declared by him for the ﬁ rst time.
The rift between extremists and moderates was resolved in
1916 A.D. Lucknow session of INC. Hence statement (2) is
incorrect. The two-nation theory was never opposed during
Lahore Congress Session, though it was opposed by the
Congress as a political party. Hence, statement (3) is also
incorrect. Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q:

questions.explanation:
In 1930 A.D., Gandhi began a protest against the salt tax
as part of his civil disobedience campaign. He was arrested
and jailed in May of 1930 A.D., so his followers marched on
the salt works at Dharsana without him. Gandhi advocated
a total non-violent form of protest, and noted that while the
marchers would be beaten at Dharsana, he urged them not
to resist, not to even raise a hand to ward off the blows. The
above is an eyewitness account of the events at the Dharsana
Salt Works as described by journalist Webb Miller.

Who of the following organized a march on the Tanjore

questions.explanation:
The Vedaranyam March or Vedaranyam Satyagraha was
organized to protest the salt tax imposed by the British
Empire in India. The march took place in April 1930 A.D.
and was the second of its kind, following the Dandi March
organized by Mahatma Gandhi, both in the framework
of the Civil Disobedience Movement. The Vedaranyam
March was a group of volunteers under the leadership
of C. Rajagopalachari. It began at Trichinopoly (now
Tiruchirappalli) and ended in Vedaranyam, a small coastal
town in Tanjore (in present day Vedaranyam beach of
Nagapatinam district). By collecting salt directly from the
sea, the marchers broke the Salt Law.

violence.

Disobedience Movement.

questions.explanation:
In 1934 AD, during the Congress Committee meeting in
Patna, the formation of the All India Congress Socialist Party
was formally recognized. In October 1934 AD, in Bombay,
the party's policies and working principles were determined.
In the same year, in Patna, Jayaprakash Narayan was one

the following statements:
1. It advocated the boycott of British goods and
evasion of taxes.
2. It wanted to establish the dictatorship of the
proletariat.
3. It advocated a separate electorate for minorities
and oppressed classes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 A.D. as a
socialist caucus within the INC. Its members rejected what
they saw as the anti-rational mysticism of Gandhi as well
as the sectarian attitude of the Communist Party of India
towards the Congress party. Inﬂ uenced by Fabianism as
well as Marxism, the CSP advocated armed struggle as well
as non-violent resistance. The CSP advocated decentralized
socialism in which cooperation, trade unions, independent
farmers and local authorities would hold a substantial share
of economic power. As secularists, they hoped to transcend
communal divisions through class solidarity. Hence, option
(d) would be the correct answer.

questions.q:
Madras (159 seats out of total 215 seats) - Congress
2. Bihar (98 seats out of total 152 seats) - Congress
3. Central Provinces and Berar (70 out of 112) - Congress
4. United Provinces (134 seats out of 228) - Congress
5. Orissa (36 out of 60 seats) - Congress
* Congress emerged as the single largest party in Bombay (86
seats out of 175), Assam and North-West Frontier Province.
Only in Bengal, Punjab and Sindh did Congress not secure
enough support from masses to form the government on its
own. The cabinets formed by Congress after 1936-37 A.D.
elections only lasted for 28 months. In July 1937 A.D.,
Congress formed cabinets in 6 provinces - Madras, Bombay,
Central Province, Orissa, Bihar, and United Province and
with the support of other parties Congress formed a coalition
government in Assam (a coalition government was formed
by Muhammad Saadulla in 1937, but later resigned and
Congress government led by Gopinath Bordoloi took ofﬁ ce in
September 1938) and North-West Frontier Provinces. Based
on 1937 results, Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Khan, formed
a coalition government although Indian National Congress was
the single largest party, the Congress formed the government
there by moving no-conﬁ dence motion against Qayyum Khan.
The inclusion of Indians into the Second World War without
consultation led to the resignation of all Congress cabinets.
On 22nd October, 1939 A.D. Congress cabinet of all provinces
resigned as an act of protest. Congress coalition government
in Assam under Gopinath Bordoloi was resigned from the
government in November, 1939 and the NWFP government
was also resigned in November, 1939. On the resignation of the
Congress cabinets, Jinnah called Indian Muslims to celebrate
22nd December, 1939 A.D. as a Day of Deliverance. *Working
Committee of Indian National Congress decided for abolition of
feudal intermediaries/peasants proprietorship in 1937 A.D. as a
result of which Congress governments in U.P. and Bihar passed
tenancy bills. Congress secured 134 seats out of 228 seats in
United Provinces and formed government on its own. *Govind
Ballabh Pant was the Prime Minister (Premier) while Kailash
Nath Katju was Law and Justice Minister and Revenue/Home/
Jail Ministry was given to Raﬁ Ahmed Kidwai. * In Congress-
ruled states the reports related to Muslims grievances were in
the following chronological order.
- Pirpur Report - 1938
- Sharif Report - March, 1939
- Fazlul Haq Report (Muslims Sufferings Under Congress
Rule Report) - December, 1939

requested the States to be handed over to the authority of
External Affairs, Defence and Communications to the Indian
Dominion. The integration of Princely states took proper
shape in his leadership.

questions.explanation:
The term "Pakistan" or Pakstan (later became Pakistan) was
ﬁ rst coined by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Pakistani nationalist
in a pamphlet published in 1933 A.D. The word was formed
by combining the names of the regions that were to constitute
the proposed nation: Punjab, Afghan Province (North-West
Frontier Province), Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan. The idea
of Pakistan gained further momentum, leading to the creation
of the independent state of Pakistan in 1947.

Muslim League at Allahabad Session in 1930. Muhammad
Iqbal said “ I would like to see Punjab, the North-West
Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan amalgamated into
a single state. Self-government within the British Empire,
or without the British Empire, formation of a consolidated
North-West Indian Muslim state appears to me to be the ﬁ nal
destiny of the Muslims, at least of North-West India.

demand 'Nothing less than complete Freedom'. Today I give

*On 8th August, 1942 A.D., Jawahar Lal Nehru presented
the ‘Quit India resolution’ to All India Congress Committee.
This proposal was supported by Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel.
The draft of this proposal was prepared by Mahatma Gandhi
himself with the help of Jawahar Lal. *Hindu Mahasabha,

Committee couldn't come to Bombay, he was arrested and
kept at Patna (Bankipur) Jail. Shivkumar and Ram-nandan
Mishra (he was ﬁ rst arrested in Cuttack but later he was
transferred to Hzaribagh). were arrested in Hazaribagh.
*Movement of 1942 showed maximum impact in Bombay,
Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, United Province of Agra and Oudh
and Madras but the participation of the whole country was
necessary for this movement to succeed. *Lord Wavell was
the commander in chief of India during Quit India Movement

to 1947 A.D. *Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of
England during Quit India Movement. *Abul Kalam Azad

ﬁ ve years (1941-45 A.D.) no session of Congress was held and

for these years. He was the President of Congress for the
maximum years before independence, also the political scenario

from different parts of Bombay Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia played
a signiﬁ cant role in the Quit India Movement. He directed the
movement while remaining underground. He also established
an undergraound radio station. *Usha Mehta was an important
member of the group of Congress that broadcasted radio being
underground. *Louis Fischer, an American journalist, was with
Gandhiji just before Quit India Movement as he came to India
in May 1942 and spent one week with Gandhiji at Sevagram
Ashram, Wardha. (He was biographer of Gandhiji).

groups of farmers performed agricultural activities in the day

strength demonstrated the glimpses of the revolt of 1857, that is
why Viceroy Linlithgow in a telegram to British Prime Minister
Winston Churchill termed this movement as by far the most
serious rebellion after the Revolt of 1857. *During the Quit
India Movement, Jayaprakash Narayan ﬂ ed from Hazaribagh
jail and became active in the underground activities. Yogendra
Shukla too ﬂ ed with J.P. Narayan on 9th November, 1942 A.D.
but was later arrested in Muzaffarpur and sent to Patna. *On
the speech given by Gandhiji during Quit India Movement
(1942 A.D.), Pattabhi Sitaramayya said, “In reality that day
Gandhiji was speaking after being motivated with the power
of Avatar and Paigambar. *Rashtriya Swayam Sevak Sangh

important feature of Quit India Movement. These were:-
1. Ballia - August 1942 A.D. - Chittu Pandey led the
Government.
2. Tamluk (Midnapore) Bengal - From December 1942 to

longest-serving Parallel Government till May 1946 A.D. Its

at Poona (now Pune). The Movement of 1942 A.D. mostly
affected the State of Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, United
Province (U.P.) and Madras. Though the whole country
participated in this Movement.

questions.q:
Which one of the following observations is not true
about the Quit India Movement of 1942?

options.B: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
options.D: It did not attract the labour class in general.

questions.explanation:
Quit India Movement of 1942 A.D. was not so non-violent.
According to ofﬁ cial assessments, in ﬁ rst week 250 railway
stations were either damaged or destroyed, and more than
500 post ofﬁ ces and 150 police stations were attacked. Heavy
violence was used for the suppression of the movement from
the ruling party. Mahatma Gandhi himself in 1942 A.D.
refused to condemn the violence. He said it was an answer
to the huge violence of the rulers. The arrest of the main
leaders (including Gandhiji) before even start of movement
had made the movement more aggressive and spontaneous.
The movement did not attract the labour class in general
(due to reasons like monetary constraints, fear of repression,
effect of trade unions etc.) in comparison to other sections
of society like students, farmers etc.
Thus, options (a) and (b) are individually not correct.

questions.explanation:

of violent means in his articles. Thus, statement 3 is not

India Movement.’

After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued
a pamphlet entitled “The Way Out.” Which one of the
following was a proposal in this pamphlet?

options.A: The establishment of a “War Advisory Council” composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States

devised a proposal in 1944 A.D. called ‘The way out’ for

Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January, 1897 A.D.
in Cuttack of Odisha division of Bengal province. He graduated

and 1939 A.D. He founded Forward Bloc in 1939 A.D. and ﬂ ed
away to Germany in 1941 A.D. In 1943 A.D., he gained control
of Azad Hind Fauz. He was given title of Netaji here.

2. He escaped from home internment in January 1941
A.D.
3. On October 21 1943 A.D. he constituted the Provincial
Government of India in Singapore.
questions.explanation:
In 1938, the 51st annual session of the Congress was held
at Haripura (Gujarat), not at Tripuri. Subhas Chandra Bose
presided over the Haripura session. The 52nd annual session of
the Congress was held at Tripuri (Madhya Pradesh) in 1939
under the presidentship of Subhas Chandra Bose; later, he
resigned from the post. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose escaped at
night from house arrest in January 1941 by disguising himself
and successfully carried out his plan to leave Calcutta. He
formed the Provisional Government of India at Singapore on
21 October 1943. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b).
In the English version of this question, “Provincial” was
mistakenly printed in place of “Provisional”; therefore, the
Bihar Public Service Commission removed this question
from evaluation.

questions.explanation:
The Indian National Army (INA) was the brainchild of
Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon along with Mohan Singh Major
Fujiwara and on 15 July, 1942 The Indian National Army was
formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh. Giani Pritam
Singh became actively involved in the Indian Independence
Movement and Gadar Party. He met with Iwaichi Fujiwara,
who had even before the declaration of war by Japan, reached
an agreement of collaboration with the Japanese at Bangkok
in December, 1941. It was Giani Pritam Singh’s idea working
with Iwaichi Fujiwara who released Indian soldiers who
were asked to join an Indian National Army to ﬁ ght for
Indian independence. These plans were started long before
the war broke out, among a group of revolutionaries based
in Bangkok. Thus, Capt. Mohan Singh was not the founder
of INA, but was only the ﬁ rst operational Commander of the
INA. He accepted the position at the insistence of Giani Ji
and Iwaichi Fujiwara. The brains behind INA were Iwaichi
Fujiwara and Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon.

Fujiwara and on 15 July, 1942 The Indian National Army was
formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh. Giani Pritam
Singh became actively involved in the Indian Independence
Movement and Gadar Party. He met with Iwaichi Fujiwara,
who had even before the declaration of war by Japan, reached
an agreement of collaboration with the Japanese at Bangkok
in December, 1941. It was Giani Pritam Singh’s idea working
with Iwaichi Fujiwara who released Indian soldiers who
were asked to join an Indian National Army to ﬁ ght for
Indian independence. These plans were started long before
the war broke out, among a group of revolutionaries based
in Bangkok. Thus, Capt. Mohan Singh was not the founder
of INA, but was only the ﬁ rst operational Commander of the
INA. He accepted the position at the insistence of Giani Ji
and Iwaichi Fujiwara. The brains behind INA were Iwaichi
Fujiwara and Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon.

Clement Attlee, the Prime Minister of United Kingdom, the
mission included Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the secretary of
state for India, Sir Stafford Cripps, President of the Board
of Trade and A.V. Alexander, the ﬁ rst Lord of the Admiralty.
Lord Wavell, the Viceroy of India, did not participate in
every step but was present. The Mission arrived on March
24, 1946 AD.
According to the Mission, the representation of the Provincial
Legislatures were to be broken up into 3 sections
(a) Section A : Madras, United Provinces, Central Province
and Berar, Bombay, Bihar & Orissa.
(b) Section B : Punjab, Sindh, NWFP
(c) Section C : Assam and Bengal.
Apart from this, the Provinces of Chief Commissioners,
Delhi, Ajmer-Marvar and Coorg will be included in category
(A) and Baluchistan will be included in category (B).
The Congress accepted the proposals related to the constitu-
ent assembly. But since, the Muslim league had been given
disproportionate representation; it rejected the idea of the
interim government.
The Muslim League ﬁ rst approved the Plan. But when
congress, declared that it could change the scheme through
majority in the Constituent Assembly they rejected the plan.
Muslim League on repeated request by Lord Wavell joined
the Interim Government on 13 October, 1946 AD.

questions.explanation:
The Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Clement Attlee
announced on 20th February, 1947 AD in the House of
Commons that he wish to transfer powers to India but also
said that if in time the decision related to the constitution is not
made British Empire has the power to transfer Government
to any of them. Thus, to effect the transfer of power, Attlee
decided to send Lord Mountbatten as Viceroy to India. Lord
Mountbatten armed with vast powers became India’s Viceroy
on 24 March, 1947 AD. Mountbatten became Viceroy of
India with a mandate to oversee the British withdrawal. Lord
Mountbatten came to India as Viceroy of India along with
speciﬁ c instructions to keep India United if possible however
he was authorized to make decisions according to favourable
Indian circumstances and minimum British loss. Mountbatten
concluded that a United India was an unachievable goal
and resigned himself to a plan for partition, creating the
independent nations of India and Pakistan.

questions.q:
The Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the
partition of the country mainly because –

options.A: The principle of Two-Nation Theory was then acceptable to them.
options.B: It was imposed by the British Government and the Congress was helpless in this regard.
options.C: They wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.
options.D: India would have otherwise lost the opportunity to attain freedom.

questions.explanation:
Attlee announced the appointment of Lord Mountbatten as
Viceroy replacing Lord Wavell. Lord Mountbatten, the last
British Governor-General and Viceroy arrived in India in
March, 1947 AD and immediately began to take measures
for the transfer of power. The prevailing communal violence
in the country led Mountbatten to announce the partition plan
on 3rd June, 1947 AD. The Congress leaders too had come
to the conclusion that partition was the only choice to check
the widespread communal violence and bloodshed that was
ravaging the country. The plan provided for the immediate
transfer of power on the basis of the grant of Dominion Status.
The Indian National Congress agreed to the partition of the
Country mainly because they wanted to avoid large-scale
communal riots.

questions.q:

the Mountbatten plan.

options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation:
Assertion (A) is correct, but reason (R) is wrong as though
INC accepted Mountbatten plan, but they never accepted
‘Two Nation Theory.’ The reason behind their acceptance
of the Mountbatten Plan was to avoid communal riots in
the country.

questions.q:
As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji
suggested to Mountbatten that he –

options.B: Invite Jinnah to form the Government.
options.C: Invite Nehru and Jinnah to form the Government together.
options.D: Invite the army to take over for some time.

questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst meeting between Gandhiji and Mountbatten took
place on 31st March, 1947 AD. As an alternative to the
partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that
the best course would be to ask Jinnah to take over as Prime
Minister of Interim Government and run the affairs of the
Country but this suggestion of Gandhiji was not acceptable to
Congress Leaders and Congress Working Committee. He told
his attendants: “Today I ﬁ nd myself all alone. Even Sardar and
Jawaharlal think that he was wrong, and peace was sure to
return if the partition was agreed upon. Nevertheless, I must
speak as I feel ... we may not feel the full impact immediately,
but, I can see clearly that the future of independence gained
at this price is going to be dark. Should the evil I apprehend
overtake India ... let posterity know what agony this old soul
went through, thinking of it.... Let it not be said that Gandhi
was party to Indian vivisection.”

questions.q:
By a Regulation in 1793, the District Collector was
deprived of his judicial powers and made the collecting
agent only. What was the reason for such regulation?

options.A: Lord Cornwallis felt that the District Collector’s efﬁ ciency of revenue collection would enormously increase without the burden of other work.
options.B: Lord Cornwallis felt that judicial power should compulsorily be in the hands of Europeans. While Indians could be given the job of revenue collection in the districts.
options.C: Lord Cornwallis was alarmed at the extent of power concentrated in the District Collector and felt that such absolute power was undesirable in one person.
options.D: The judicial work demanded a deep knowledge of India and a good training in law and Lord Cornwallis felt that District Collector should be only a revenue collector.

questions.explanation:
Cornwallis judicial reforms took their ﬁ nal shape in 1793
AD and were embodied in the famous Cornwallis Code.
The new reforms were based on the principle of Separation
of Powers. Under the inﬂ uence of the eighteenth-century
French philosophers Cornwallis sought to separate the
revenue administration from the administration of justice. The
Collector was the head of the revenue department in a district
and also enjoyed extensive judicial and magisterial powers.
Cornwallis believed that concentration of all powers in the
hands of the Collector in the District retards the improvement
as a judge of the Diwani Adalat redress the wrongs done by
him as collector or assessor of revenue? Thus, neither the
landlords nor the cultivators could regard the Collector as
an impartial Judge in revenue cases. The Cornwallis Code
divested the Collector of all judicial and magisterial powers
and left him with the duty of administration of revenue. A
new class of ofﬁ cer called the District Judge was created to
preside over the District Civil Court. The District Judge was
empowered with magisterial and police functions.

questions.q:
The real intention of the British to include the Princely
States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act
of 1935 was to –

options.A: Exercise more direct political and administrative control.
options.B: Involve the princes actively in the administration of the colony.
options.C: Finally effect the complete political and administrative take-over of all the princely States by the British
options.D: Use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders.

questions.explanation:
The real intention of the British to include the Princely
States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of
1935 was to use the princes to counter balance the anti-
imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders. Princely States
represented approx 25% of the population of India while
under the Government of India Act, 1935 out of 260 members
156 were to represent the provinces and 104 to the Princely
States in the Upper House and the Lower House consisted
of 375 members out of whom 250 were to represent the
provinces and 125 to represent the Princely States. In both
Houses of the Federal Legislature, the states were given their
quota of representation. But the members from the State were
not to be elected. Despite such a wide range of provisions, the
princely states however refused to join the Federation. They
were alarmed by the changing situation in the country caused
by the rapid spread of the National Movement. The British
Government miserably failed to overcome the opposition of
the Indian National Congress, the Muslim League and the
princes against the Federal Scheme. So the Federal Scheme
was withheld except the establishment of the Federal Court
and the Provincial scheme was introduced on 1st April, 1937
causing a drastic change in the pattern of provincial politics.

questions.q:
Which of the following famines of the 19 century in
th
India has been described as ‘Sea of Calamity’?
questions.explanation:
Orissa (Odisha) Famine of 1866-67 AD in India has been
described as ‘Sea of Calamity.’ The impact of the famine,
however, was greatest in Odisha, which at that time was quite
isolated from the rest of India. In Odisha alone, at least 1.3
million (13 lakh) people, a third of the population died in
1866 due to starvation and diseases.

questions.q: The Indian Famine Code, 1883 was prepared by –
questions.explanation:
The Indian Famine Code, 1883 was prepared by Strachey
Commission. Strachey Commission was appointed in
1878 AD to formulate general principles and measures for
prevention of The Great Famine of 1876-78 AD.

questions.q:
Which of the following commissions are related to
famine in British India ?
1. Campbell Commission
2. Lyall Commission
3. Strachey Commission
4. Hunter Commission
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
questions.explanation:
1. Campbell Commission – This commission was con-
stituted in 1866, to investigate the causes of famine
(especially in connection with the then Orissa famine)
and to suggest measures for prevention and relief.
2. Lyall Commission – This commission examined
famine conditions and suggested relief-related mea-
sures (it is associated with the famine inquiry after the
1896–97 famine).
3. Strachey Commission – This commission was consti-
tuted after the Great Famine (1876-78) to frame policy
and principles for dealing with famines and became an
important basis for famine relief planning/codes.
4. Hunter Commission – This commission was not a
famine commission; it was mainly related to educa-
tion (and “Hunter Commission” is also used for a later
inquiry of a different context).

questions.q:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
List- I (Period) List- II
A. AD 1767 - 69 1. First Anglo-Maratha War
B. AD 1790 - 92 2. Third Mysore War
C. AD 1824 - 26 3. First Anglo-Burmese War
D. AD 1845 - 46 4. Second Sikh War
Code :
questions.explanation:
First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82 AD) - The internal
problems of the Marathas and the growing ambition of
the English brought the beginning of the Anglo-Maratha
struggle. The primary cause of the ﬁ rst Maratha war was the
interference of the English Government at Bombay in the
internal affairs of the Marathas. The First Anglo-Maratha War
ended with the Treaty of Salbai signed between the Mahadaji
Scindia and the Warren Hastings in 1782 AD. In the Treaty
of Salbai, status quo was maintained which gave the British
20 years of peace with the Marathas.
Third Anglo- Mysore War (1790-92 AD)– It was
fought between British and Tipu Sultan. British attacked
Srirangapatnam with the help of Nizam and Marathas. Under
the leadership of William Medows, British defeated Tipu
Sultan and they had a treaty in Srirangapatnam in March,
1792 AD. According to this treaty, Tipu Sultan was to give
away half of his kingdom and he had to pay 3 crores to British
for damages done in the war.
The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26 AD) – The
ﬁ rst of three wars fought between the British and Burmese
Empires in the 19th century. The war which began primarily
over the control of northeastern India, ended in a decisive
British victory, giving the total British control of Assam,
Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia as well as Arakan Province
and Tenasserim. The Burmese were also forced to pay an
indemnity of one million pounds, and sign a commercial
treaty ‘Treaty of Yandabo’.
Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49 AD)-The Second Anglo-
Sikh War took place in 1848 and 1849 between the Sikh
Empire and the British East India Company.

questions.q:
Consider the following events and arrange them in
chronological order from earliest to latest:
1. Vellore Mutiny
2. Death of Nana Phadnavis
3. Recall of Wellesley
4. Anglo-Nepalese War
Choose the correct answer from the options given
below:
questions.explanation:
On July 10, 1806 AD, a military uprising took place at the
Vellore Fort in Tamil Nadu, known as the Vellore Mutiny. The
mutiny was caused by several social, religious, and political
factors, particularly British policies and their disregard for
Indian soldiers' sentiments.
Nana Phadnavis, a prominent political leader of the Maratha
society, passed away in March 1800 AD. Lord Wellesley
served as Governor-General from 1798 AD to 1805 AD.
Due to his aggressive expansionist policies and military
campaigns, the British government faced ﬁ nancial difﬁ culties
and recalled him in 1805 AD.
Lord Hastings (1813–1823 AD) later oversaw the Anglo-
Nepalese War (1814–1816 AD), which concluded with the
Treaty of Sugauli.

questions.explanation:

Battle of Wandiwash (1760) – A decisive battle fought
between the British and the French during the Third
Carnatic War. This is the earliest among the four.
Death sentence awarded to Raja Nandkumar (1775) – Raja
Nandkumar, a hindu Brahmin and former landlord of Berhampur,
was tried on charges of forgery and hanged at Calcutta.
Treaty of Salbai (1782) – The agreement between the East
India Company and the Marathas at the end of the First Anglo–
Maratha War (1775–1782) is called the Treaty of Salbai.
Death of Tipu Sultan (1799) – Tipu Sultan, the ruler of
Mysore, was killed during the Battle of Srirangapatnam in
the Fourth Anglo–Mysore War (1799).

questions.explanation:

(1919-24 AD) was a movement of Indian Muslims, led by
Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali and supported by Mahatma

1916 AD and September 1916 AD, respectively, by Indian
nationalist Bal Gangadhar Tilak and British social reformer
Annie Besant.
Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (April 13, 1919 AD) - incident
occurred on April 13, 1919 AD, in which British troops ﬁ red on
a large crowd of unarmed Indians in an open space known as
the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar in the Punjab region (now in
Punjab state) of India, killing thousands people and wounding
many thousands more. Hence option (a) is correct answer.

questions.q:
Match the correctly –
A. Child marriage 1. Ishwarchand Vidyasagar
B. Suppression of 2. Colonel Sleimen
Thuggee
C. Widows’ Remarriage 3. M.G. Ranade
D. Suppression of 4. Lord Hastings
Pindaris
Code :
A B C D
questions.explanation:
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is considered one of the pillars
of the Bengal Renaissance. In other words, he managed to
continue the reforms movement that was started by Raja
Rammohan Roy. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar initiated the
concept of Widow Remarriage and he also opened the doors
of colleges and other educational institutions to lower caste
students, which were earlier reserved only for Brahmins. For
his immense generosity and kind-heartedness, people started
addressing him as “Daya Sagar” (ocean of kindness). Major-
General Sir William Henry Sleeman was a British soldier
and administrator in British India, best known for his work
on suppression of thuggee. Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade
was a judge, politician, writer and reformer of India. He was
also an active reformer. He set up the Social Conference
Movement, which worked against child marriage, Widows
Remarriage, spending heavily in marriages and other social
functions. Ranade advocated for widow remarriage and
female education. Lord Hastings became Governor-General in
1813. Lord Hastings ﬁ nally decided to suppress the Pindaris.
Hastings planned vigorous military preparations to surround
the Pindaris from all sides - on the north and east from Bengal,
on the west from Gujarat and the south from the Deccan. A
massive army of 113,000 men and 300 cannons was divided
into two parts - on the northern side under Hastings’ command
and the southern under the control of Thomas Hislop. By the
end of 1817, the British troops were successful in expelling
the Pindaris from Malwa and across the Chambal. In January,
1818 the Pindaris were practically exterminated.

misgovernment or oppression. He wrote: “Political freedom

speciﬁ cally criticizing the policies of Congress towards
colonial rule in India.

questions.q:
With reference to Lala Lajpat Rai which of the
following statements is/are correct?
1. At ﬁ rst he was not in favour of the policy of Non-
cooperation but later he joined in favour of Gandhi.
2. Lala Lajpat Rai also participated in the formation
of Swaraj Party.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below.
questions.explanation:
Initially Lala Lajpat Rai was not in favour of the non-
cooperation movement, because he was not satisﬁ ed with the
policies of prayer, persuasion and humility of the Congress.
But later in September 1920 AD, the Congress held a special
session in Calcutta under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai
and a resolution was passed to run the Non-cooperation
Movement. Hence statement 1 is true. The Non-cooperation
Movement was called off by Gandhiji on February 4, 1922
AD after Chauri Chaura incident. Angered by incident C.R.
Das and Pandit Moti Lal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in
January 1923 AD. Lala Lajpat Rai also joined this party but
in June 1925 AD after death of C.R. Das, Lala Lajpat Rai
and Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya left the party. Hence both
statements are true.

discarded the wig hitherto regarded as mandatory for formal
occasions and to presided over the House, wearing a Gandhi
cap. When asked by the Britishers in this context, he said:
“Your wig is not suitable for this warm climate.” He also
became the ﬁ rst Speaker of Lok Sabha.

British Raj. He was one of the key organizers of the Indian
National Army (INA).

questions.q: Who gives the slogan ‘Jai Jawan’, Jai Kisan’ ?
questions.explanation:
‘Jai Jawan Jai Kisan’ (English: Hail the Soldier, Hail the
Farmer) was a slogan given to India by the then Prime
Minister of India, Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1965, at a public
gathering at Ramlila Maidan, New Delhi.

questions.q: The present day calendar is based on :
questions.explanation:
Most prevalent calendar in the present-day is Gregorian
Calendar. It is used worldwide.

questions.q: Bhartiya Kisan Sangh was established in which year?
questions.explanation:
Bhartiya Kisan Sangh was established on 4th March 1979 AD
at Kota, Rajasthan by Dattopant Thengdi.
questions.note: The book marks this answer with (*), indicating the answer is disputed/ambiguous among the given options; see the explanation.

questions.q:
Who said, “Freedom is almost within reach, we have
to seize it ?”
questions.explanation:
At the time of Quit India Movement which was started
on August 9,1942 AD, Mahatma Gandhi said: “Freedom
is almost within reach, we have to seize it.” On the same
occasion, Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of “Do or Die.”

questions.q:
Who of the following had written, “India’s salvation
will not be achieved under the leadership of Mahatma
Gandhi”?
questions.explanation:
Writing in his much-acclaimed book ‘The Indian Struggle’,
Subhash Chandra Bose stated, “Mahatma Gandhi has
rendered and will continue to render phenomenal service to
his country.” “But,” he added, “India’s salvation will not be
achieved under his leadership.”

questions.q:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Most of the early nationalists considered
British rule as an act of providence destined to bring
modernisation.
Reason (R): They complained only against "Un-British
rule" in India.
Choose the correct answer from the options given
below:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
options.C: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.explanation:
A signiﬁ cant portion of the early nationalist leaders viewed
British rule in India as a tool ordained by divine will
(Providence), which was necessary to bring modernization
to India. They believed that British rule facilitated
industrialization, education, administrative facilities, and
other reforms that paved the way for the development of
Indian society. However, their criticism was limited to the
"Un-British rule" in India, rather than British rule as a whole.
Thus, both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are true, and
Reason (R) also correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.q:
“Everything else can wait, but not agriculture.” The
above statement is attributed to :
questions.explanation:
After Independence, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru stated that
“Everything else can wait, but not agriculture.”

questions.q:
In which year was the ﬁ rst cloth mill established in
Bombay?

options.E: None of these

questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst Indian cotton cloth mill was established in 1818 AD
at Fort Gloaster (Kolkata), but it failed. The ﬁ rst successful
modern cloth mill was established in Bombay (Mumbai) in
the year 1854 AD, was the ﬁ rst cotton textile mill of Bombay.
It was established by a Parsi cotton merchant Cowaszee
Nanabhoy Davar.

questions.q:
"Kings are made for Public; Public is not made for the
King." Who among the following made this statement
during the National Movement?
questions.explanation:
“Kings are made for Public; Public is not made for the
King”. This statement was made by the Grand Old Man of
India, the well-known industrialist, educationist and thinker
Dadabhai Naoroji.

questions.q:
The founder of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides Movement
in India was –
questions.explanation:
On 1 August, 1907 AD, Robert Baden-Powell took a diverse
group of 20 adolescents to Brown Sea Island in Dorsetshire
where they set up camp for a fortnight. It was a great success
and the start of Boy Scouts and Civil Guides Movement in the
United Kingdom. Just after that, in 1908 AD the Boy Scouts
Movement began in all over the world with the publication of
the ﬁ rst installment of Robert Baden-Powell’s 'Scouting for
Boys.' Thus, Baden Powell is considered the founder of Boy
Scouts and Civil Guides Movement in India. In India scouting
was introduced in 1909 and guiding in 1911.

questions.q:
In the context of Indian history, the Rakhmabai case
of 1884 revolved around
1.women's right to gain education
2. age of consent
3. restitution of conjugal rights
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Rakhmabai was one of the ﬁ rst practicing women doctors in
colonial India. She was also involved with a landmark legal
case involving her marriage as a child bride between 1884
AD and 1888 AD. This case led to the enactment of the Age
of Consent Act in 1891.

questions.q:
With reference to Indian freedom struggle, which one
of the following statements in not correct?

options.A: The Rowlatt Act aroused a wave of popular indignation and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre
options.B: Subhash Chandra Bose formed the Forward Bloc
options.C: Bhagat Singh was one of the founders of Hindustan Republican Socialist Association
options.D: In 1931, the Congress Session at Karachi opposed Gandhi-Irwin Pact

questions.explanation:
The First Round Table Conference could not produce any
fruitful result. The main reason was the absence of Congress
from the Conference. The Government started to convince
the Congress to participate in the Second Round Table
Conference in 1931 AD. Finally, Gandhiji was convinced
to negotiate with the Viceroy Lord Irwin. So Gandhiji and
Lord Irwin met on February 19th, 1931 and after discussion
of ﬁ fteen days, they signed an agreement on March 5 , 1931
th
known as “Gandhi-Irwin Pact.” In 1931, the Congress session
at Karachi, approved the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Thus, statement
(d) is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jawaharlal
Nehru:
1. He was the president of the Congress Party in 1947
2. He presided over the Constituent Assembly
3. He formed the ﬁ rst Congress Ministry in United
Province before India’s Independence
Of these statements:
questions.explanation:
None of the above statements about Jawaharlal Nehru is correct
because Jivatram Bhagwandas Kriplani was the president
of the Congress Party in 1947 AD. The ﬁ rst meeting of the
Constituent Assembly took place on 9th December 1946 AD.
Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was its interim president. Dr.
Rajendra Prasad was elected as its permanent president on 11th
December, 1946 AD. He was not included in the ﬁ rst Congress
Ministry in United Province before India’s independence.

questions.q:
The statement “I am a socialist and a republican and
am no believer Kings and Princes” is associated with
questions.explanation:
“I am a socialist and a republican and do not believe in Kings
and Princes” this statement is associated with Jawaharlal
Nehru.

questions.q:
Who among the following has been described as the
high priest of Communism in India?
questions.explanation:
Nehru’s ideas contained analysis and interpretation of
socialism, including Marxism. An interesting role in this
connection was played by the Publicity Department of the
United Provinces which depicted Nehru as a communist. This
was done through a pamphlet entitled ‘Communistic Likes
and Dislikes.’ In this, Nehru was described as a high priest
of Communism in India. But it was a propaganda against
Nehru. In fact, the Government wanted to confuse the public
about Nehru’s socialistic views. But the high ups in authority
advised to stop such attempts and not to identify him with
the Communists.

questions.q:
Who became champion of socialism and wanted to
overthrow British rule, Princely states, Landlordism
and Capitalism in 1933?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Jawaharlal Nehru was a supporter of socialism. Nehru wanted
to overthrow British rule, Princely states, Landlordism and
capitalism in 1933 AD. Nehru's socialism was inﬂ uenced
by the socialism of the Soviet Union. He visited the Soviet
Union in November, 1927 AD.

questions.q:
Who one of the following is the biographer of Jawahar
Lal Nehru?
questions.explanation: Frank Moraes was the biographer of Jawaharlal Nehru.

questions.q:
Ambabai, a woman freedom ﬁ ghter, belonged to which
of the following States of India?
questions.explanation:
Amba Bai was born in the erstwhile Mysore state (now in
Karnataka). She became a widow at very young age. After
getting inspiration from Gandhi, she picketed foreign cloth
and liquor shops in Udipi during Salt Satyagraha.

questions.q: The Sarabandi Campaign of 1922 was led by :

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Bardoli in Gujarat (Surat District) became hub of political
activities in 1928 AD. Bardoli's Mehta brothers (Kalyan ji
and Kunwar Ji) and Dayalji Desai started a movement in
support of farmers from 1928 AD. Afterward this movement
was led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Under the leadership
of Patel, Sarabandi Campaign (No-tax) was also launched
in 1928. Although the year 1922 AD is incorrectly given in
the question.

questions.q:
Of the four forms of political protests mentioned below,
which one is derived from the name of the person who
used it as a political weapon for the ﬁ rst time?
questions.explanation:
Boycott word is derived from the name of Captain Charles C.
Boycott, an Irish land agent. He was the ﬁ rst one who used
this as a political weapon in 1880 AD.

questions.q:
Who of the following was sent as a representative of
labourers by Indian Government to the Washington
Summit of I.L.O. in the year 1919?
questions.explanation:
International Labour Organisation (ILO) came into existence
in the year 1919 AD. N.M. Joshi was sent as a representative
of labourers to the first summit of I.L.O. held in the
Washington in the year 1919 AD. B.P. Wadia was sent as his
advisor to this summit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875.
2. ‘Al Hilal’ was published by Maulana Abul Kalam
Azad.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai was not associated with the paper
‘The People.’
4. The famous Presidency College (formerly Hindu
College) of Calcutta was established by Raja Ram
Mohan Roy.
Of these statements :
questions.explanation:
The Arya Samaj was founded by Maharishi Swami
Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 AD. ‘Al Hilal’ was an Urdu
weekly newspaper published by Maulana Abul Kalam in
1912 AD. The famous Presidency College (formerly Hindu
College) of Calcutta was established by Raja Ram Mohan
Roy in collaboration with David Hare in 1817 AD. Lala
Lajpat Rai was associated with the paper 'The People'. Hence
statement (c) is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following events and arrange these in
chronological order –
I. Assassination of Curzon Wyllie
II. Execution of Khudiram Bose
III. Starting of 'Kesari' newspaper by Bal Gangadhar
Tilak
IV. Starting of 'Al Hilal' newspaper by Abul Kalam
Azad
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Assassination of Curzon Wyllie – 1909 AD
Execution of Khudiram Bose – 1908 AD
Starting of 'Kesari' by Bal Gangadhar Tilak – 1881 AD
Starting of 'Al Hilal' by Abul Kalam Azad – 1912 AD

questions.q:
Of the following events, which stands third in
chronological order?
questions.explanation:
The correct chronological order of the events is :
Champaran Movement - 1917 AD
Non-Co-operation Movement - 1920-22 AD
Dandi March - 1930 AD
Quit India Movement - 1942 AD
Thus, Dandi March stands at the third position in chronological
order.

questions.q:
Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
Person Associated with
questions.explanation:
James Augustus Hicky started a weekly newspaper in
1780 named “Hicky’s Bengal Gazette” (also known as
“The Original Calcutta General Advertiser”). He was not
associated with the Calcutta Chronicle. Dayanand Saraswati
wrote the famous work ‘Satyarth Prakash’. E. V. Ramaswamy
Naicker (Periyar Ramaswami Naicker) was a leader of the
Dravidian movement and the ‘Self-Respect Movement’
in South India, and later joined the Justice Party. Jyotirao
(Jyotiba) Phule founded the ‘Satyashodhak Samaj’ in 1873.

questions.q:
With reference to the British Colonial rule in India,
consider the following statements :
1. Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in the abolition
of the system of 'indentured labour'.
2. In Lord Chelmsford's 'War Conference', Mahatma
Gandhi did not support the resolution on recruiting
Indians for World War.
3. Consequent to the breaking of Salt Law by Indian
people, the Indian National Congress was declared
illegal by the colonial rulers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
Indentured labourers were those who were taken out of India
as labourers for ﬁ xed periods in the British colonies. Their
condition was like that of bonded labourers. Gandhiji ﬁ rst
raised his voice in favour of indentured labourers in South
Africa in 1894 AD. In the year 1914 AD, by the Gandhi's-
Smuts Agreement, the tax of 3 pounds on these labourers
ended. After coming back to India, Gandhi negotiated with
Viceroy Lord Chelmsford to end the indentured system and
ﬁ nally in July 1917 AD the indentured system was banned.
Thus statement (1) is correct. After Gandhiji's Dandi March
and his breaking of salt law on April 6, 1930 AD, Indians
across the country started violating the salt law. In response to
this, many Congress leaders and Satyagrahis like Jawaharlal
Nehru, Mahadev Desai etc. were sent to prison and Indian
National Congress was declared illegal by British rule. Thus
statement (3) is correct.

questions.q:
Which lady contributed the most to Indian politics
after 1947?
questions.explanation:
Aruna Asaf Ali was an Indian independence activist and a
freedom ﬁ ghter. She participated in the Quit India Movement
from underground. After India’s independence, she became
associated with the left socialist group, which merged with
the Communist Party of India in 1955 AD.

questions.q:
“It will be our blunder if we leave people of Bihar
and their Government unsafe before the violence and
uncivilized attacks of league leaders.” In the year 1946
who told this?
questions.explanation:
The above statement was made by Sardar Patel in 1946, with
reference to the riots in Bihar.

questions.q:
Who raised the demand of ‘Complete Independence’
for the ﬁ rst time in 1921?
questions.explanation:
Maulana Hasrat Mohani was one of the greatest leaders in
India. He fought against the British Government for freedom.
Maulana Hasrat Mohani raised the demand for Complete
Independence for the ﬁ rst time in 1921.

questions.q:
Who has hailed Mohd. Ali Jinnah most responsible for
the partition of India?
questions.explanation:
Lord Mountbatten (1947-48) hailed Mohd. Ali Jinnah most
responsible for the partition of India. Lord Curzon was the
Viceroy of India from 1899 to 1905. Lord Linlithgow was
the Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943. Lord Irwin was
appointed as the Indian Viceroy in April, 1926 and continued
his ofﬁ ce till 18 April 1931.

questions.q:
Who amongst the following presided over the All
Parties Muslim Conference held in Delhi on 31st
December, 1928?
questions.explanation:
Aga Khan, also known as Maulana Sultan Mohammed Shah
presided over the All Parties Muslim Conference in Delhi
from December 31, 1928 AD to 1 January 1929 AD. All
India Muslim Conference was set up under the leadership of
Aga Khan and demanded separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.q:
The Banaras Session of August, 1923 of the Hindu
Mahasabha was presided over by :
questions.explanation:
The Banaras Session of August, 1923 AD of the All India
Hindu Mahasabha was presided over by Pandit Madan
Mohan Malviya, which was attended by around 1500
delegates including Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and Parsis.

questions.q: Who is considered as the creator of Modern Bihar?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Sachchidananda Sinha was an Indian lawyer, parliamentarian
& journalist. He was born in Arrah, then Bengal Presidency
(in present-day Bihar). He began a movement for a separate
province of Bihar with a small group of people. It was realized
in 1912 AD with the formation of the Bihar (carved out of
Bengal presidency).

questions.q:
Identify the years those are closest to the founding of
the Communist Party of India and the RSS respectively.
questions.explanation:
Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) was founded on
September 27, 1925 AD in Nagpur by Keshav Baliram
Hedgewar, while Communist Party of India was founded in
December 1925 AD in Kanpur. Atal Bihari Vajpayee is the ﬁ rst
Swayamsevak to become Prime Minister of India.

questions.q: The real name of the ‘Frontier Gandhi’ is :
questions.explanation:
Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a Pashtun independence
activist and a spiritual leader nicknamed as “Frontier Gandhi”
due to his political activities and close association with the
Indian leader, Mahatma Gandhi. He was a lifelong paciﬁ st
who advocated non-violent opposition and founded the
Khudai Khidmatgar to protest against the British-controlled
army using peaceful protests and political activism. He was
awarded Bharat Ratna in 1987.

questions.q: Who is known as 'Frontier Gandhi'?

options.E: None of the above/More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a Pashtun independence
activist and a spiritual leader nicknamed as “Frontier Gandhi”

Indian leader, Mahatma Gandhi. He was a lifelong paciﬁ st
who advocated non-violent opposition and founded the

questions.q:
Who among the following is popularly known as the
‘Frontier Gandhi?
questions.explanation:
Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan was a Pashtun independence

questions.q:
Who among the following are known as 'Bombay
Trimurti'?
questions.explanation:
Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji were
known as the 'Bombay Trimurti'. Together, in 1885 A.D., they
founded Bombay Presidency Association.

questions.q:
What was the name of the movement started by Khan
Abdul Gaffar Khan against British?
questions.explanation:
Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) had organized a
volunteer brigade 'Khudai Khidmatgars' popularly known as
the 'Red Shirts' who were pledged to the freedom struggle and
non-violence during civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q:
'Khudai Khidmatgar' (Servants of God) was established
by:
questions.explanation:
Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) had organized a
volunteer brigade 'Khudai Khidmatgars' popularly known as
the 'Red Shirts' who were pledged to the freedom struggle and
non-violence during civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q:
Who of the following attacked on Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
by saying:
Ambedkar has had his leadership thrust upon him by
a benign British Government because his services were
necessary to embarrass the Nationalist leaders.’
questions.explanation:
Dr. B.S. Moonje was a Hindu nationalist leader. He made the
above-statement in 1932 AD, due to the demand for a separate
electorate for Dalits raised by B.R. Ambedkar.

questions.q:
How did the study of history help in creating a feeling
of nationalism in India towards the end of the 19th
century?

options.A: By urging people to struggle and change the miserable conditions of life under the British rule
options.B: By reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of Indians as backward, primitive and incapable of governing themselves
options.C: By writing about India's glorious past and urging people to take pride in their achievements
options.D: More than one of the above
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation:
The study of history helped in creating a feeling of nationalism
in India towards the end of 19th century by -
- Urging people to struggle and change the miserable
conditions of life under British rule.
- Reinterpreting history and refuting the British portrayal of
Indians as backward, primitive and incapable of governing
themselves.
- Writing about India's glorious past and urging people to
take pride in their achievements.

questions.q:
The native State of Tripura became involved in the
Freedom Movement early in the 20th century because:

options.A: The kings of Tripura were always anti-British
options.B: The Bengal revolutionaries took shelter in Tripura
options.C: The tribes of the state were ﬁ ercely freedom loving
options.D: There were already some groups ﬁ ghting against the kingship and its protector, the British

questions.explanation:
King of the princely State of Tripura involved educated
Bengalis in his administration. Due to pressure from the
Britishers in the early twentieth century, some of the Bengal
revolutionaries had taken shelter in Tripura, which resulted
in the expansion of Independence Movement in Tripura.

questions.q: Rajendra Prasad belonged to :
questions.explanation:
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was born on December 3, 1884 in Ziradei
village in Siwan district of Bihar. He was the ﬁ rst President
of Independent India. He was the permanent President of the
Constituent Assembly that drafted the Constitution.

questions.q: Women Saint Daya Bai was a disciple of –
questions.explanation:
Women saint Daya Bai was a disciple of Saint Charandas.
She wrote a book named 'Dayabodh'.

questions.q:
The great poet Rabindranath Tagore emerged as a
great painter, when he was –
questions.explanation:
Great poet Rabindranath Tagore emerged as a great painter at
the age of 70 years. Tagore was the ﬁ rst Indian artist to exhibit
his works in 1930 across Europe, Russia, and the United
States of America, earning him critical acclaim in the West.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements :
1. St. Francis Xavier was one of the founding
members of the Jesuit Order.
2. St. Francis Xavier died in Goa and a church is
dedicated to him there.
3. The Feast of St. Francis Xavier is celebrated in Goa
each year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation:
St. Francis Xavier arrived in Goa in 1542 AD. He was
instrumental in spread of Christianity in India and was one of
the founding members of Jesuit order. He died on December
3,1552 on a Shangchuan Island (China). Hence statement 2 is
incorrect. The feast of St. Francis Xavier is celebrated every
year on 3rd December in Goa.

questions.q: Jagat Narain Lal was sent to :
questions.explanation:
Jagat Narain Lal was sent to Hazaribagh Jail during the
freedom struggle. After the release of Jagat Narain Lal on
July 14, 1929 AD, Rajendra Prasad addressed a meeting in
Gulabbag, Patna.

questions.q:
The Samadhis of Kasturba and Mahadev Desai are
situated in the premises of :
questions.explanation:
The Samadhis of Kasturba and Mahadev Desai are situated
in the premises of Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

questions.q:
The tomb of Kasturba Gandhi is situated in the
premises of :
questions.explanation:
The Samadhis of Kasturba and Mahadev Desai are situated
in the premises of Aga Khan Palace, Pune.

questions.q:
Who among the following was the author of the ofﬁ cial
history of Congress?
questions.explanation:
Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was a nationalist and an important
leader of the freedom struggle. He was the author of the
ofﬁ cial history of Congress and 'Gandhi and Gandhism'. He
is famous for his defeat by Subhash Chandra Bose in congress
session of Tripuri, 1939 AD.

questions.q:
During the colonial period in India, what was the
purpose of the Whitley Commission?

options.A: To review the ﬁ tness of India for further political reforms
options.B: To report on existing conditions of labour and to make recommendations
options.C: To draw up a plan for ﬁ nancial reforms for India
options.D: To develop a comprehensive scheme for Civil Services in India.

questions.explanation:
The Royal Commission, better known as the Whitley
Commission, was asked to report and make recommendations
on “the existing conditions of Labour in industrial
undertakings and plantations in British India, on the health,
efﬁ ciency and standard of living of the workers and on the
relations between employers and employees.”

questions.q:
What was the common relationship between Katherine
Mayo, Aldous Huxley, Charles Andrews and William
Digby?

options.A: They wrote commentaries on the condition of India during the British rule
options.B: They were supporters of the Indian National Movement
options.C: They were opponents of the Indian National Movement
options.D: They were friends of Mahatma Gandhi

questions.explanation:
Katherine Mayo was an American historian and nativist
known for her polemical book Mother India (1927). Aldous
Huxley was an English writer and philosopher. Charles Freer
Andrews was a social reformer in India. He was also one of
the best friends of Mahatma Gandhi. William Digby (May
1, 1849 - 29 September, 1904) was a British author and
journalist. The common relationship between all of them
is that they wrote commentaries on the condition of India
during the British rule.

questions.q:
The year of Bengal Famine in which millions of people
died is :
questions.explanation:
The Bengal Famine of 1943 AD was a large famine in
Bengal, a State in British-ruled India, claiming the lives of
approximately 3.0 million people.

questions.q:
To establish global peace and cooperation among
the peoples, which of the following concepts was
introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, played a crucial
role in setting the national agenda. He introduced the concept
of Non-Alignment to establish peace and cooperation among
people. The three major objectives of Nehru’s foreign
policy were to preserve the hard-earned sovereignty, protect
territorial integrity and promote rapid economic development.
Nehru wished to achieve these objectives through the strategy
of Non-Alignment. The roots of Non-Alignment Movement
(NAM) goes back to the friendship between three leaders –
Yugoslavia’s Josip Broz Tito, India’s Jawaharlal Nehru, and
Egypt’s leader Gamal Abdel Nasser. Indonesia’s Sukarno and
Ghana’s Kwame Nkrumah strongly supported them. These
ﬁ ve leaders came to be known as the ﬁ ve founders of NAM.
The ﬁ rst non-aligned summit was held in Belgrade in 1961.

questions.q:
Which part of India remained under Portuguese
control after 15th August, 1947?
questions.explanation:
After 15 August, 1947 AD, Goa remained under Portuguese
th
control. In 1955 AD America supported the claim of the
Portuguese Government over Goa. Operation Vijay was
conducted by Indian forces to free Goa from Portuguese
control. The armed action which involved the Indian Army,
Navy and Air Force was a decisive victory for India, ending
approximately 450 years of Portuguese rule in India on 19th
of December, 1961 AD.

questions.q:
Against which colonial power did the freedom struggle
have to continue in India even after 15 August, 1947?
questions.explanation:
After 15 August, 1947 AD, Goa remained under Portuguese
th
control. In 1955 AD America supported the claim of the
Portuguese Government over Goa. Operation Vijay was
conducted by Indian forces to free Goa from Portuguese
control. The armed action which involved the Indian Army,
Navy and Air Force was a decisive victory for India, ending
approximately 450 years of Portuguese rule in India on 19th
of December, 1961 AD.

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is not true for
Jawaharlal Nehru?

options.A: He was inﬂ uenced by Socialism.
options.B: He was inﬂ uenced by British liberalism.
options.C: He was inﬂ uenced by Mahatma Gandhi.
options.D: He was inﬂ uenced by German Nationalism.

questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst Prime Minister of India Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
was inﬂ uenced by socialism, British liberalism and also by

questions.q:

Conference took place.
2. Indian Navy Revolt, 1946 took place when the
Indian sailors in the Royal Indian Navy at Bombay
and Karachi rose against the Government.
Which one of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India when Shimla
Conference took place. Thus, statement 1 is false. One of
the most spectacular episodes of the intense revolt against
the British Raj was the uprising of the sailors of the British
Indian Navy in 1946 AD. On February, 18 the sailors and
shipmen of the Royal Indian Navy battleship 'HMIS Talwaar,'
who were at the time posted to the Bombay harbour, went on
strike. They were protesting against the bad food and adverse
conditions. After the assurance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
On 24 February, 1946 AD, the rebels were ready to surrender.
Thus, statement 2 is correct.

2. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was the ﬁ rst
graduate of the Calcutta University.
3. Keshav Chandra Sen’s campaign against sati led
to the enactment of law to ban sati by the then
Governor-General.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar encouraged women's education
and opened 35 women's schools in Bengal. Pandit Ishwar
Chandra Vidyasagar was the first secretary of Bethune
School and its management committee was formed under
his chairmanship. Thus statement 1 is correct. The famous
Bengali novelist, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was one
of the ﬁ rst two graduates from Calcutta University in 1858.
Thus, statement 2 is also correct. Due to the campaign of
Raja Ram Mohan Roy against Sati system, Governor-General
Lord William Bentinck banned the Sati system by The Bengal
Sati Regulation, 1929. Thus, statement 3 is incorrect and the
desired answer will be option (b).

announced in the year :
questions.explanation:
The first Industrial Policy in independent India was
propounded on April 6, 1948 AD in the proposal of industrial
policy. The concept of a mixed economy for India was ﬁ rst
framed in this policy. Under this, the public and private
sectors were divided, and both were allocated different
industries. The main aspect of the Industrial policy of 1948
AD was that it made an attempt to clarify the role of the public
and private sector in industrial development.

questions.q:

questions.explanation:

movement, involved a cyclical approach of alternating
between phases of active resistance (struggle), temporary
truces or negotiations, and resuming the struggle with
renewed determination if the objectives remained unfulﬁ lled.
Although BPSC has deleted this question in its ﬁ nal answer
key as it has accepted that during civil disobedience
movement this strategy was most prominently used.

The Gandhi–Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931.
The pact opened the way for participation of Congress/
Gandhi in the Second Round Table Conference, which was
held in London from September to December 1931.
The Poona Pact was concluded on 24 September 1932, under
which, in place of a separate electorate for the “Untouchables/
Dalits,” the provision of a joint electorate with reserved seats
was decided.
The Civil Disobedience Movement is formally considered
to have ended at the A.I.C.C. Patna session held on 18–19
May 1934.

(d) is the correct answer.

questions.explanation:
During the Second World War, in protest against Britain's
inclusion of India in the war without Indian consent, Congress
ministers resigned in October 1939 AD. Subsequently, the
53rd session of the Congress was held in March 1940 AD at
Ramgarh (present-day Jharkhand), presided over by Maulana
Abul Kalam Azad.
In August 1940 AD, the British government introduced the
"August Offer" (or Linlithgow offer) to seek Indian support
for the war. Later, in 1942 AD, the Cripps Mission was sent
to India. This mission proposed limited self-governance
for India and was part of a series of efforts to secure Indian
cooperation in the war effort.

questions.explanation:
Gandhi, the exponent of the Satyagraha Movement, staged
his first Satyagraha in Champaran, Bihar (in 1917). In
the Champaran of Bihar, the cultivators were forced by
Europeans to grow indigo, a blue dye and this imposed on
them untold sufferings. They could not grow the food they
needed, nor did they receive adequate payment for the indigo.
Gandhi decided to start his ﬁ rst Satyagraha for the cause of
the peasants. Rowlatt Act was passed in March, 1919 by the
British Government while Jallianwala Bagh massacre took
place on April 13,1919 AD in which British troops ﬁ red on
a large crowd of unarmed Indians in Amritsar in the Punjab
of India, killing nearly thousand people and wounding many
hundreds more. The Chauri-Chaura episode took place on
February 4, 1922 AD, just after this incident, Mahatma
Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.q:
The objective of the Butler Committee of 1927 was
to :

options.A: Deﬁ ne the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments.
options.B: Deﬁ ne the powers of the Secretary of State for India.
options.C: Impose censorship of the national press.
options.D: Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.

questions.explanation:
The Indian State Committee constituted a committee in the
year 1927 under the Chairmanship of Sir Harcourt Butler,
also known as the Butler Committee. The formation of this
Committee was about the investigation and classiﬁ cation
of relationship between the Supreme power and the Native
kings. The Committee visited 16 states and submitted its
report in the year 1929. After examining the existing relations
of Supreme (British) power in Indian and princely states the
Committee presented its recommendations regarding the
ﬁ nancial and economic relation of these two.

questions.q:

by the Indian Princely States abolished?
questions.explanation:
Privy purse was a payment made to erstwhile Indian princely
states' ruling families by central government of India as part
of their agreement to merge their states with the Republic of
India in 1949 thereby ending their ruling rights. However all
the special rights and privy purse enjoyed by Indian Princely
States were abolished by 26th Constitutional Amendment Act,
1971 in the year of 1971.

top most independent business unions also participated.

questions.q:

the help of which one of the following theories?

help of dialectical materialism. According to Marx, in the
process of historical chronology, "Slavery" was the base
of ancient society. "Land" was the base of Feudal Society
and "Capital" was the base of middle-class society. It is his
"Materialistic description of History" According to Marx,
the history of society is determined by economic causes that
inherit class struggle.

Rabindranath Tagore during the Bengal partition movement
of 1905. The music of this song is inspired by the melody
of the Hymn ‘Ami Kothay Pabo Tare’ written by Gagan
Harkara. Bangladesh adopted the ﬁ rst 10 lines of this song as

English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the
National Anthem of India ‘Jana Gana Mana’. He is the only
poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as
the national anthem of the two countries.

in dance and dramatics called Tribhanga has been a
favourite of Indian artists from ancient times till today.

this pose?

options.A: One leg is bent and the body is slightly but oppositely curved at waist and neck

questions.explanation:

is the correct answer.

questions.q:
With reference to Dhrupad, one of the major traditions
of India that has been kept alive for centuries, which
of the following statements are correct?
1. Dhrupad originated and developed in the Rajput
kingdoms during the Mughal period.
2. Dhrupad is primarily a devotional and spiritual
music.
3. Dhrupad Alap uses Sanskrit syllables from Mantras.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation:
Dhrupad is the Indian classical music that traces its origin to
the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras. It was originated
by King of Gwalior Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516). Hence,
Dhrupad was originated way back before Mughal Period. Hence
statement 1 is wrong. It is also primarily a form of worship, in
which offerings are made to the divine through sound. Thus
Statement 2 is correct. Dhrupad is performed in two parts- Alap
and Bandish. In the Alap, the singer uses syllables from Sanskrit
Mantras. Therefore, statement 3 is correct.

2. It cannot be traditionally witnessed by the higher
caste Hindus

4. Its theatre form is called Koothambalam
Which of these statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Chakiarkoothu is an art form in which the stories of Hindu
mythology and epics are orally rendered primarily. Only the
members of the Chakiar community performed this art form
and hence the name Chakiarkoothu. This was performed in
temple theatre called Koothambalam. An accompanying artist
plays the percussion instrument mizhavu in the background.

questions.q:
With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the
following statements:
1. It is a song and dance performance.
2. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in
the performance.
3. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds of
Lord Krishna.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Manipuri Sankirtana is one of the few important Indian heritage
inscribed on the UNESCO representative list of the intangible
cultural heritage of humanity. It is a form of performing art
involving virtual singing, drumming and dancing which are
performed in the temples and domestic spaces in Manipur state.
Through the performances which exhibit unparalleled religious
devotion and energy, the performers narrates the life and deeds
of Lord Krishna. So, statements 1 and 3 are correct. Since the
Kartal and Pung are also used, statement 2 is incorrect.

questions.explanation:

It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India.

questions.q:
With reference to the famous Sattriya dance, consider
the following statements:
1. Sattriya is a combination of music, dance and
drama.
2. It is a centuries-old living tradition of Vaishnavites
of Assam.
3. It is based on classical Ragas and Talas of devotional
songs composed by Tulsidas, Kabir and Mirabai.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Sattriya dance is one of the eight principal classical Indian
dance traditions. Recognized in 2000 as a classical dance
by Sangeet Natak Akademi. The Sattriya is the most recent
entrant on this list. The Sattriya dance form was introduced
by the Great Vaishnava saint and reformer of Assam,
Mahapurusha Sankaradeva as a powerful medium for the
propagation of the Vaishnava faith. It is a centuries-old
living tradition of Vaishnavites of Assam. Sattriya Nritya
is accompanied by musical compositions called Borgeet
(composed by Sankardeva and Shree Shree Madhavdev
among others) which are based on classical ragas.

questions.q:
Which one of the following dances involves solo
performance?
questions.explanation:
In the above options, Mohiniattam involves solo performance.
Mohiniattam is a classical dance form from Kerala, India.
It is considered as a graceful form of dance meant to be
performed as solo recitals by women. The Mohiniattam
dance focuses mainly on feminine moods and emotions.
Usually, the theme of Mohiniattam dance is “sringara” or
love. Subtle subjects of love are executed with suggestive
abhinaya using subtle gestures, rhythmic footwork and
lilting music. The legend of Vishnu as “Mohini,” (the
enchantress) forms the core of Mohiniattam dance.

questions.q:

questions.explanation:
The latest cultural heritage of India included in the UNESCO’s
Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of
Humanity is Garba, a traditional dance form from Gujarat in
December, 2023. Garba is a ritualistic and devotional dance
that is performed on the occasion of the Hindu festival of
Navaratri, which is dedicated to the worship of the feminine
energy or 'Shakti'.
Chhau dance, Durga puja in Kolkata and Kumbh mela
were included in the UNESCO’s Representative List of the
Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, 2021 and
2017 respectively.

questions.q:
How do you distinguish between Kuchipudi and
Bharatanatyam dances?
1. Dancers occasionally speaking dialogues is found in
Kuchipudi dance but not in Bharatanatyam.
2. Dancing on the brass plate by keeping the feet on its
edges is a feature of Bharatanatyam, but Kuchipudi
dance does not have such a form of movements.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst statement is correct as Kuchipudi is a famous folk
dance of Andhra Pradesh. It presents more realistic acting
occasionally including dialogue spoken by the dancers.
Another unique feature of Kuchipudi is the Tarangam, in
which the performer dances on the edges of a brass plate,
executing complicated rhythmic patterns with dexterity, while
sometimes also balancing a pot of water on the head. So, the
second statement is incorrect. The correct answer is option (a).

questions.q:
Which one of the following is not the factor of ‘Cultural
Lag’?
questions.explanation:
The term refers to the notion that culture takes the time
to catch up with technological innovations and that social
problems and conﬂ icts are caused by this lag. According to
Ogburn, cultural lag is a common societal phenomenon due
to the tendency of the material culture to evolve and change
rapidly. Cultural lag is seen as a critical ethical issue because
failure to develop broad social consensus on appropriate
applications of modern technology may lead to a breakdown
in social solidarity and the rise of social conﬂ ict.

questions.q: Identify the wrong pair related to Indian Cinema:

options.D: First Indian Cinemascope Film - Kagaz Ke Phool

questions.explanation:
The ﬁ rst Indian ﬁ lm to be nominated for an Oscar was
‘Mother India’ (released in 1957) directed by Mehboob Khan.
The ﬁ lm failed to win the award in Best Foreign Language
Film (Best International Feature Film) category. Keechak
Vadham released in 1918 was the ﬁ rst full-length Tamil silent
ﬁ lm. The ﬁ lm was directed by Nataraja Mudaliar.
The technique of playback singing was ﬁ rst used in 1935 in
the ﬁ lm ‘Dhoop Chhaon’ directed by Nitin Bose. The ﬁ lm was
a remake of Bengali ﬁ lm ‘Bhagya Chakra’. The technique of
playback singing was in fact ﬁ rst used in ‘Bhagya Chakra.’
